_comment: SHARED cross-implementation conformance table for the ADR-0017 `materializes-when` grammar.
One tiny boolean language — `always | <clause> [(and|or) <clause>]...`, clause = `p == v | p != v
| p in [v, ...]` — is implemented THREE times, and a divergence between them fails OPEN in a
direction no single side can detect (.github#292/#266): the shell union gate
Fsgg.Registry). This table pins them together so the NEXT grammar tweak on one side reds a test
instead of shipping a wrong union gate into a scaffolded product.
Each fixture is (predicate, params) -> expected bool. The harness (conformance.sh) asserts BOTH:
(a) the shell evaluator returns `expected` for (predicate, params); and
(b) it still returns `expected` for (normalize_when(predicate), params) — i.e. the Python
normalizer never changes the evaluated meaning (the quoted-literal fail-open shape #292).
An `unparseable: true` fixture instead asserts the shell evaluator rejects it (exit 2).
This file is the CONTRACT, not a shell/Python artifact: FS.GG.Contracts' typed Fsgg.Registry
validator should assert the same table (see the cross-repo item filed from #398) so all three
implementations are pinned to one truth.

fixtures.note: quoted literal compares by INNER bytes — the #292 fail-open leg
a literal containing a comma must NOT be split — normalize must preserve it verbatim
and it is the WHOLE literal, not a prefix
no-space list — normalize regularizes spacing, meaning unchanged
and: both hold (feedback bool stringified to the token `true`)

fixtures.predicate: profile == governed and feedback == true or profile == game
fixtures.note: precedence: OR of ANDs — (governed AND true) OR (game) = true

fixtures.predicate: profile == governed and feedback == true or profile == minimal

fixtures.note: absent param reads empty ⇒ == is false
absent param reads empty ⇒ != is true
unknown operator ⇒ the evaluator dies (exit 2), not a silent false
